original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Prove the exact eight-call minimum for the PR2085 four-target endpoint after adding one arbitrary symmetric rational rank-one address, including signed scaling and any finite number of restored dirty roles with free address-independent binary mixing.
scope_change_reason: Explicit user-selected follow-up to PR6032 Open next questions. This is a scoped formal alphabet barrier, not the original card's larger/nonabelian native supplier construction. It removes one proposed escape without claiming a paid supplier or kappa gain.
bottleneck_link: Side result: one scaled rank-one extension cannot improve the eight-call formal primitive. Two-frame alphabets or changed endpoints remain possible; native implementation and complete paid invoices are separate obligations.
stop_rule: Stop after a self-contained proof, independent exact count/support/rank verification, meaningful controls and one focused package; stop earlier if a gap invalidates the theorem. Do not launch broader word searches.
evidence: README.md gives the arbitrary-R/all-finite-width proof. verify.py and independent.py check 462 count profiles, 40 determinant candidates/20 frames, 160 support conditions, four survivors/four rank obstructions, six exact words at widths 4/5/7, 49 rejected mutations, two longer-word witnesses and three additional failure controls and two hand-computed noncommuting products. Source hashes and normal/optimized registered replay are checked. Universal claims rest on the proof, not finite fixtures.

open_questions.question: Can two added rational rank-one frames beat eight calls for the same endpoint?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the next alphabet extension suggested by PR6032 and is not excluded by the one-frame theorem.
open_questions.first_step: Use the joint determinant equation and target-support constraints for at most seven calls; test the first-order equations only for surviving multiplicities.
open_questions.blocked_by: No joint universal classification or exact saving word is supplied. Native implementation and a full paid invoice are required before any multiplication-bound use.

open_questions.question: Which positive rank-one frames can occur in exact words of arbitrary length?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The minimum-eight theorem does not classify all possible extra-frame use; reciprocal old-frame subdivisions have explicit longer words.
open_questions.first_step: Remove the seven-call cap from the determinant/support/rank argument and classify positive frames, beginning with reciprocal old-frame subdivisions.
open_questions.blocked_by: An all-length classification and its certificate are not provided in this package.
